record.original_question: Given a finite term-rewriting system, is it decidable whether the set of its ground normal forms is a regular tree language?

evidence.quote: Is it possible to decide whether the set of ground normal forms with respect to a given (finite) term-rewriting system is a regular tree language?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let Σ be a finite ranked alphabet and let T(Σ) denote the set of ground (variable-free) terms over Σ. A term-rewriting system (TRS) over Σ is a finite set R of rewrite rules ℓ → r, where ℓ and r are terms (possibly with variables) over Σ and Var(r) ⊆ Var(ℓ). A ground term t ∈ T(Σ) is called a ground normal form (with respect to R) if no rule of R can be applied to any subterm of t, i.e., no subterm of t is an instance of any left-hand side ℓ of a rule in R. Let NF_R ⊆ T(Σ) denote the set of all ground normal forms of R. A set L ⊆ T(Σ) is called a regular tree language if it is recognized by some finite (bottom-up) tree automaton.

Decide the following problem: given as input a finite term-rewriting system R over a finite ranked alphabet Σ, determine whether the set NF_R of ground normal forms of R is a regular tree language. In other words, is the property "NF_R is a regular tree language" decidable as a function of the finite TRS R?
artifact.status_search_result: The decidability of whether the set of ground normal forms of a finite term-rewriting system is a regular tree language has been established. Work by Vágvölgyi and Gilleron (e.g., "Decidability of regularity and related properties of ground normal form languages", CTRS 1992 / Inform. and Comput. 1995) reduces the regularity test to a decidable finite-irreducibility property, showing that the question is decidable.

status_evidence.title: Decidability of Regularity and Related Properties of Ground Normal Form Languages (Information and Computation)
status_evidence.snippet: Testing regularity of the language of ground normal forms can be reduced to checking a finite irreducibility property, proving the decidability of regularity of the set of ground normal forms.
status_evidence.claim: The regularity of the set of ground normal forms of a finite TRS is decidable.

status_evidence.title: Decidability of regularity and related properties of ground normal form languages (SpringerLink)
status_evidence.snippet: Conference paper establishing decidability of regularity of ground normal form languages for term rewriting systems.
status_evidence.claim: Decidability result published, resolving the open problem.
